notes: Kuhn's equation κλέος ἄφθιτον = śrávas ... ákṣitam; Watkins 1995 ch. 15 frame PRO(dat) + BE + IMPERISHABLE FAME. The dative 1st-person pronoun stands in both (Gk μοι sg., Ved. asmé pl.; singular follows Greek). The verb 'be' is Greek only (Ved. has dhehi): interpolated; the Greek future is rendered by the PIE subjunctive.

plan.english: Place imperishable fame on us for a lifetime!

notes: Watkins 1995 ch. 15: god as subject, PRO(dat) + *dʰeh₁- + *ḱléwos *n̥dʰgʷʰitom + *h₂oyu- (EVER). Krisa and Timocreon are quoted from Watkins/West, not a local corpus. *h₂óyu is secure only at root level: Ved. viśvā́yu- is a compound epithet, Gk αἰϝεί a locative of the same stem; rendered as the locative 'in (one's) lifetime'. Aorist imperative follows Ved. dhehi; Timocreon's τίθει is a present stem.

plan.english: He places imperishable fame upon himself.

notes: Watkins 1995 ch. 15: man as subject, PRO(nom) + *dʰeh₁- MIDDLE + imperishable fame. Ved. dhatte is the reduplicated present middle; Herodotus (quoted from West 2007 ch. 10) has the middle aorist of the same root; the present stem follows Vedic. Ved. ákṣiti- is the i-stem variant of the adjective; Il. 9.413 supplies the exact ἄφθιτος. The emphatic pronoun follows Ved. sá.

plan.english: May he hold imperishable fame for a lifetime.

notes: The Krisa votive verse (7th c., from Watkins 1995 ch. 15): '(that) he too may have imperishable fame forever'. *seǵʰ- (ἔχω) is Greek only and interpolated; Vedic expresses the same frame with dhatte (see fame-003). *h₂óyu is a root-level match (αἰϝεί : viśvā́yu-), rendered as a locative 'in a lifetime'. Optative as in ἔχοι.

máhi śrávaḥ = μέγα κλέος (West 2007 ch. 10; formula *méǵh₂ ḱléwos). The beneficiary dative stands in both (Ved. asmé, Gk αὐτῇ), but the Greek verb is renewed (ποιεῖτ(αι) 'makes for herself'), so *dʰeh₁- is Vedic-only here and interpolated.

κλέος εὐρύ against Ved. urugāyám ... śrávaḥ 'wide-going fame' (West 2007 ch. 10; West ch. 2 on renewal by pṛthú). *h₁wérHus is secure only as the first member urú- of the Vedic compound. The enclitic pronoun follows Ved. naḥ; the verb is Vedic only (Od. 3.83 has μετέρχομαι).

plan.english: We heard the fames of men.

notes: κλέα ἀνδρῶν 'the famous deeds of men' (West 2007 ch. 10): Ved. nṛṇā́m ... śrávaḥ has the same genitive plural of *h₂nḗr with *ḱléwos (singular there; the Vedic plural śrávāṃsi of deeds, RV 3.30.5, supports the plural); Old Irish (quoted from West) has cloth (*ḱlutom, same root) with nert (*h₂ner-to-). The verb 'hear' (*ḱlew-, figura etymologica) is interpolated: Greek has πεύθομαι, 1st plural as in the Greek.

plan.english: The king, seeking fame, goes forth.

notes: Ved. śrávaḥ icchámāna- 'seeking fame' (RV 1.110.5, 1.126.1, 6.58.3, 10.102.4) and the Lay of Igor's slavy iskati 'to seek fame' (West 2007 ch. 10; text not in a local corpus) share the *sḱé-present of *h₂eys- 'seek'; Slavic slava is an o-grade derivative of *ḱlew-, so *ḱléwos is secure at root level. The middle participle follows Vedic. 'King' (RV 1.126.1), 'goes forth' (RV 10.102.4 éti prá) are Vedic only and interpolated.

plan.english: May you place good fame on me.

notes: *h₁wésu ḱléwos 'good fame' (West 2007 ch. 10): Av. vohu sravah-, OIr fó chlú (Laws, quoted from West); Greek renews the adjective (κλέος ἐσθλόν) and supplies only *ḱléwos. The Avestan prayer to Fire (Y. 62.6) has the optative 2sg dāiiā̊ with enclitic mē; Av. dā- continues *dʰeh₁- and *deh₃- alike, so the verb is interpolated (aorist optative of *dʰeh₁- 'place', as in the 'grant fame' frame). Avestan puts the fame in the locative; accusative object here.

plan.english: Now may I win good fame.

notes: Achilles' resolve (Il. 18.121) and Diomedes' (Il. 5.3): win good fame in battle (West 2007 ch. 10 'Fame won in combat'). 'Good' is secure through Av. vohu and OIr fó (Greek renews it with ἐσθλόν). The verb *h₂er- 'take, win' (ἄρνυμαι, aorist optative middle ἀροίμην, matched exactly) is Greek only and interpolated. nu follows Gk νῦν.

śrútyaṃ nā́ma = ὄνομα κλυτόν (West 2007 ch. 10; Tocharian A ñom-klyu 'name-fame' as a compound). Greek κλυτός is exactly *ḱlutós; Ved. śrútya- is a -ya- derivative of the same root, so *ḱlutós is secure at root level. 'Bears' follows Ved. bíbhrat (participle there) and is interpolated.

Odysseus' false self-introduction 'to me (is) the famous name Aithon' (Od. 19.183) and Indra 'famous by name' (RV 8.46.14), West 2007 ch. 10. Dative of possession follows Greek; the copula (nominal sentence in both) is interpolated; ḱlutós as predicate.

plan.english: He placed a name on the son.

notes: *h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁- 'place a name' (West 2007 ch. 10): Hitt. lāman dāi- (ŠUM-an is the Sumerogram; dāiš is phonetic), Ved. nā́ma dhā-, Gk ὄνομα θέσθαι, Lat. nomen indere (in-dō < *dʰeh₁-). Hittite and Latin have the dative of the person named (-ši, mihi); 'the son' is interpolated (Appu names his son; the Greek name-givers are mother and grandfather). Aorist active follows Hittite preterite and Latin perfect; Greek has the middle.

Naming formula with the 3sg imperative of *h₁es- and a dative of the person: Hitt. ŠUM-an ēšdu 'let his name be (Bad)', Gk Ὀδυσεὺς ὄνομ' ἔστω 'let (his) name be Odysseus' (Autolycus naming his grandson). Both passages give a proper name; 'this' stands in for it and is interpolated.
